subject: Dedicated Capacity: GPU pool sizing, autoscale & region selection for HorizonAnalytics
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Intro + context: HorizonAnalytics Dedicated capacity ask

Hi Jonas / Dev,

Looping you in for the Dedicated capacity onboarding planning for HorizonAnalytics (contact: Alex Morgan). They committed to a Reserved Dedicated pool for Q1 2027 as part of the renewal and want predictable latency for inference workloads. Key constraints below:

- Expected steady-state: ~180 concurrent inference streams, avg seq length 512 tokens.
- Peak bursts: up to 2.5x for short windows (30–45 min) during business hours.
- Primary region: us-west (preferred), fall-back us-east.
- Data residency: model inputs include PII; customer requires VPC deployment + audit logs retention 365d.

Attachments: Horizon_Estimated_Usage.csv (usage model), Draft_SOW_Horizon_Dedicated_v1.pdf (high-level SOW).

Requesting:
1) Preliminary GPU pool sizing recommendation for steady + burst capacity (NVidia H100 equivalence).
2) Suggested autoscaling policy (min/max pool, surge/burst behavior) that meets 99th percentile latency SLO of 250ms for 512-token outputs.
3) Any network/VPC prerequisites we should share with Horizon's infra team for kickoff.

Timeline: customer wants a kickoff the week of Nov 22 to align procurement and start configuration. Can we target an internal scoping call this week?

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + context: HorizonAnalytics Dedicated capacity ask

Thanks Monica — good summary. I'm available for a scoping call Thu 11/19 or Fri 11/20.

Initial thoughts:
- Steady-state for 180 concurrent streams @ 512 tokens: conservative baseline is a 12-GPU H100-equivalent pool (mixed precision), with headroom for autoscaling to ~30 GPUs for burst phases. That assumes optimized batching (dynamic batching window ~50ms) and KV cache reuse where possible.
- Recommend defining autoscale as: min = 12 GPUs, target = 18 GPUs for sustained increases, max burst = 30 GPUs with warm-up prefetch during known peak windows. Burst should be gated by a token-rate threshold and circuit-breaker to prevent runaway scale.
- Region: prefer provisioning in us-west-2 for reduced tail latency; keep replica set in us-east-1 for cross-region fallback.

Action items:
- Dev: can you confirm memory/throughput for our quantized Llama-variant at seq 512 under continuous batching to validate numbers?
- Marissa: will coordinate kickoff and customer expectations (runbook + staging window).
- Monica: share customer's internal maintenance windows and CIDR blocks for VPC peering.

I'll sketch a quick runbook and send by EOD.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success (Dedicated)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + context: HorizonAnalytics Dedicated capacity ask

On Wed, Nov 17, 2026 at 09:10 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial thoughts:
> - Steady-state for 180 concurrent streams @ 512 tokens: conservative baseline is a 12-GPU H100-equivalent pool...

Confirmed: with our latest kernel selection and int8 quant path, a single H100-equivalent instance (using 80GB memory profiles) can sustain ~16 concurrent low-latency inferences at 512 tokens with batching. So 12 GPUs maps to ~192 concurrent sessions (aligns w/ your steady-state).

Notes:
- If customer requires more deterministic p95 latency, we should reduce batching windows for that subset of routes and reserve a small "low-latency" pool (2-3 GPUs) pinned for critical traffic.
- For burst scaling to 30 GPUs, we recommend pre-warming using a lightweight synthetic workload from our control plane to reduce cold-start tail latency.
- Network: we need NAT egress ranges and VPN / VPC peering details. Also request their security team to whitelist Redwood control-plane IPs for deployment orchestration.

I'll produce a short sizing table and a proposed autoscale policy doc and attach by EOD tomorrow.

— Dev
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@horizonanalytics.com>, procurement@horizonanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-19T07:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity: GPU pool sizing, autoscale & region selection for HorizonAnalytics

Thanks for the quick responses — appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 180 concurrent streams number is a conservative average; some product-led demos will spike to ~450 users for short periods (10–30 minutes). We need confidence the system will tolerate that without user-facing degradation.
- Preference for us-west (primary). For compliance reasons we want all logs retained for 365 days and routed to our Splunk instance.
- We can provide VPC peering and CIDR blocks — we'll put that in the kickoff doc. Procurement expects a final SOW + pricing by Nov 30 to complete budget sign-off.

We'll be ready for a kickoff on Mon Nov 22 at 10:00am PT. Please confirm attendees and dial-in.

— Alex
Director, Platform Engineering, HorizonAnalytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity: GPU pool sizing, autoscale & region selection for HorizonAnalytics

Alex — confirmed for Mon 11/22 10:00am PT. I'll host the kickoff and cover the following agenda:

1) Introductions & roles (10m)
2) Usage profile review + traffic patterns (15m)
3) Proposed GPU pool topology (baseline, target, burst) & autoscale rules (20m)
4) Network/VPC requirements & security checklist (15m)
5) Rollout plan: staging -> validation -> cutover (20m)
6) Next steps & SOW timeline (10m)

Please bring the CIDR blocks and a point of contact for Splunk integration. I'll share dial-in and a short pre-read (runbook + sizing table) by COB today.

Attachments: net-diagram-horizon.png (network sketch).

See you Monday — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Agenda and pre-read attached; thanks for the quick kickoff.

Thanks for running the session — short summary from our infra/security team:

- CIDR blocks for peering: 10.40.0.0/16 (app), 10.41.0.0/16 (management).
- Splunk ingestion endpoint and auth: we'll send a token via secure portal.
- Procurement has initial comments on the SOW; they requested clearer rollout acceptance criteria (performance tests & p95 targets) before sign-off.

Next items we will deliver by Nov 27: updated CIDR + VPN details, procurement comments, and a preferred maintenance window (Sundays 02:00–06:00 PT).

Claire Zhao
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, HorizonAnalytics
